name: Mizoram
summary: Known as the 'Land of the Hill People'. Boasts the highest percentage of forest cover among Indian states (over 85%). Famous for its Cheraw (bamboo dance) and peaceful Mizo Accord (1986).
festivals: Chapchar Kut, Mim Kut, Pawl Kut
monuments: Solomon's Temple (Aizawl), Vantawng Falls (highest waterfall in Mizoram, 229m), Phawngpui Blue Mountain
nationalParks: Murlen National Park, Phawngpui National Park (Blue Mountain)
schemes: Handholding Scheme (Bana Kaih), SEDP (Socio-Economic Development Policy)

mcqs.q: Which famous traditional folk dance of Mizoram involves dancers stepping in and out between pairs of horizontal bamboo staves?
mcqs.exp: Cheraw is an ancient dance of Mizoram where male performers rhythmically clap bamboo poles while female dancers step skillfully in between.

mcqs.q: What is the highest mountain peak in Mizoram, affectionately known as the 'Blue Mountain'?
mcqs.exp: Phawngpui (elevation 2,157 m) is the highest peak in Mizoram, reverentially called the Blue Mountain.

subtopics.name: Geography
subtopics.summary: Location, borders, physical terrain, and major river systems of Mizoram.

facts.title: Capital & Geographic Scope
facts.content: The capital is Aizawl. Mizoram covers a geographic area of 21,081 sq km across 11 administrative districts.

facts.title: Major Rivers & Drainage Systems
facts.content: Key river systems flowing through the region include: Tlawng, Chhimtuipui (Kaladan), Tut, Tuivawl.

facts.title: Geographical Landscape & Highlights
facts.content: Known as the 'Land of the Hill People'. Boasts the highest percentage of forest cover among Indian states (over 85%). Famous for its Cheraw (bamboo dance) and peaceful Mizo Accord (1986).

subtopics.name: History & Culture
subtopics.summary: Historical formation, classical/folk dances, and vibrant festivals of Mizoram.

facts.title: State Formation & Language
facts.content: Mizoram was formally instituted on 20 February 1987. Official language(s): Mizo, English.

facts.title: Dance Forms & Traditional Arts
facts.content: Celebrated traditional and folk dance forms: Cheraw (Bamboo Dance), Khuallam, Chheihlam, Chai.

facts.title: Major Festivals & Celebrations
facts.content: Prominent cultural festivals: Chapchar Kut, Mim Kut, Pawl Kut.

subtopics.name: Government & Polity
subtopics.summary: Constitutional leadership, administrative structure, and state symbols of Mizoram.

facts.title: Governor & Constitutional Head
facts.content: The current Governor is Hari Babu Kambhampati.

facts.title: Chief Minister & Administration
facts.content: The Chief Minister of Mizoram is Lalduhoma.

facts.title: High Court Jurisdiction
facts.content: Judicial jurisdiction falls under Gauhati High Court (Aizawl Permanent Bench).

facts.title: Official State Symbols
facts.content: State Animal: Himalayan serow | State Bird: Mrs. Hume's pheasant | State Flower: Red vanda | State Tree: Iron wood (Herse).

subtopics.name: Economy & Agriculture
subtopics.summary: Natural resources, minerals, industrial clusters, and agriculture in Mizoram.

facts.title: Mineral Wealth & Natural Resources
facts.content: Principal minerals and resources: Sandstone, Limestone, Clay.

facts.title: Economic Profile & Industries
facts.content: Mizoram plays a vital role in India's economy through key agricultural production, manufacturing corridors, and services.

subtopics.name: Places, Monuments & Tourism
subtopics.summary: Heritage landmarks, national parks, and tourism attractions in Mizoram.

facts.title: Historic Monuments & Cultural Sites
facts.content: Prominent monuments and heritage landmarks: Solomon's Temple (Aizawl), Vantawng Falls (highest waterfall in Mizoram, 229m), Phawngpui Blue Mountain.

facts.title: National Parks & Protected Areas
facts.content: Key protected conservation areas: Murlen National Park, Phawngpui National Park (Blue Mountain).

subtopics.summary: Prominent welfare schemes, civic initiatives, and state honors of Mizoram.

facts.title: Key State Welfare Schemes
facts.content: Notable welfare initiatives and government programs: Handholding Scheme (Bana Kaih), SEDP (Socio-Economic Development Policy).
